'''Sosigenes''' is a [[Lunar craters|lunar]] [[impact crater]] on the west edge of [[Mare Tranquillitatis]]. Its diameter is 17 km. It was named after ancient Greek astronomer [[Sosigenes of Alexandria]].<ref>{{gpn|5653}}</ref> It lies to the east of the large walled plain [[Julius Caesar (crater)|Julius Caesar]]. The crater rim has a high [[albedo]], making it relatively bright. It has a small central rise at the midpoint of the floor.

To the east on the [[Lunar mare|mare]] is a formation of parallel [[rille]]s designated the Rimae Sosigenes. These follow a course to the north, and have a length of about 150 kilometers. The small, bowl-shaped crater Sosignes A lies across one of these rilles.

==Satellite craters==
By convention these features are identified on lunar maps by placing the letter on the side of the crater midpoint that is closest to Sosigenes.
